title: Basis of the Surplus a Savings Account May Move Out
content:
The surplus a savings or money market account of Savings & Money Market Accounts may move out on the owner's instruction is what the available balance carries above the balance the account must retain.

The surplus available to move out is fixed only after the credit owed for the excess withdrawal fees charged on branch and ATM withdrawals stands on the account.

**The settled balance** is the total of the deposits, interest credits and fee refunds posted to the account less the withdrawals and fees posted to it, taken as no less than zero.

**The available balance** is the settled balance.

**The balance the account must retain** is the tier's minimum daily balance waiver threshold.

**The surplus** is the available balance less the balance the account must retain, taken as no less than zero, and the whole surplus is moved. No withdrawal already posted is set against it.

**The amount moved** is rounded half up to the cent, never less than 100.00 USD, and never more than the transfer ceiling of 5000.00 USD.

### Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a savings account whose posted totals are deposits of 30000.00 USD, interest credits of 50.00 USD and fee refunds of 10.00 USD against withdrawals of 6000.00 USD and fees of 40.00 USD, held on a tier whose minimum daily balance waiver threshold is a hypothetical 4000.00 USD.

The settled balance is 30000.00 USD plus 50.00 USD plus 10.00 USD less 6000.00 USD less 40.00 USD, that is 24020.00 USD, and the available balance is the same 24020.00 USD. The balance the account must retain is 4000.00 USD, so the surplus is 20020.00 USD and the whole of it is moved.

The amount is already at the cent. It is not below 100.00 USD, so it is not raised; it is above the transfer ceiling of 5000.00 USD, so the amount moved is 5000.00 USD.
